meta.title: CloverProof — Field-specific fertilizer decisions, with proof
meta.description: CloverProof turns your field and soil-test data into a fertilizer plan — what, how much, when and why — reviewed by an agronomist and recorded in a proof document. Vendor-neutral, software only.

hero.title: A clearer plan for every field.
hero.lead: CloverProof connects your soil tests, field history and crop goals into one fertilizer plan — what to apply, how much, when, and why — checked by an agronomist before it reaches you.
hero.note: Early-stage product. Pilot availability depends on location and fit.
hero.figureCaption: Every recommendation is tied to one field, one season and one set of inputs.
hero.imageAlt: Young winter wheat in long rows at sunrise, with clover leaves in the foreground

problem.title: The practical problem
problem.intro: Fertilizer decisions are often made from scattered records and general advice, with no trace of the reasoning.

items.title: Records live in different places.
items.body: Lab reports in email, spreader logs in a notebook, crop history in someone's memory. Nothing is joined up for the field in front of you.

items.title: Advice is generic — or tied to a product.
items.body: Blanket rates ignore the field. Advice from a supplier is shaped by what they sell. Neither shows its working.

items.title: No record of why.
items.body: When a season goes well or badly, there is nothing to look back on: which inputs were used, which assumptions were made, who signed off.

how.title: How it works
how.intro: Four steps, the same every time. Nothing reaches you without a person checking it.

steps.title: Farm data
steps.body: Your field, crop, target yield and previous crop. A lab soil test if you have one — with its method, depth and date.

steps.title: Engine
steps.body: A transparent calculation runs against a versioned set of regional rules. Every number gets a written reason and a confidence level.

steps.title: Agronomist review
steps.body: An agronomist approves, adjusts or rejects the plan. Any change is saved as a new version with the reason — the original is never overwritten.

steps.title: Proof document
steps.body: You receive a plan document: what, how much, when and why, with the reviewer, the versions used and a digital fingerprint.

proof.title: What a proof document shows
proof.intro: A sample layout. Values are left blank on purpose — real values only appear once an agronomist has reviewed your field.
whyLines: Crop need for the target yield, from the regional rule set.
Supply already in the soil, from the lab test.
proof.disclaimer: A proof document records what was recommended and why. It is not a certification and is not issued or endorsed by any third party.

items.title: Vendor-neutral
items.body: We don't sell fertilizer and we don't take commissions on it.

items.title: Software only
items.body: No sensors or hardware to buy. We work from your field information and lab results.

items.title: Confidence on every number
items.body: Each recommendation is marked high, medium or low confidence, with the reason.

items.title: No soil test, nitrogen only
items.body: Without a lab test we only advise on nitrogen, and recommend a test for phosphorus and potassium.

items.title: Every edit is versioned
items.body: Plans are never overwritten. Changes are saved as new versions with who changed what, and why.

items.q: Do I need sensors or special equipment?
items.a: No. CloverProof is software only. We work from your field details and, where available, a laboratory soil test.

items.q: What if I don't have a soil test?
items.a: We can still advise on nitrogen, at medium confidence at most. For phosphorus and potassium we'll recommend getting a test first.
Every plan is approved by a human agronomist before you see it. Automated checks never replace that review. If the agronomist changes a number, the reason is recorded.

items.q: What is the proof document for?
items.a: It's your record of what was recommended, on what inputs, and why. It is not a certification and no third party has endorsed it.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: How CloverProof collects, uses and protects the details you share when you request a pilot plan.

sections.p: The 2027 pilot is open to farms in Ontario, Canada. You can send a request from anywhere, but we can only include Ontario farms.

When you request a pilot plan we collect what you enter: name, email, country, approximate farm size, main crop, plus the language you used and the exact consent wording you agreed to, with the time. If you join the pilot we also collect farm, field and soil-test information and the plans we make for you.
To decide whether we can include your farm in the pilot, to contact you about it and, if you join, to make and record your fertilizer plans. We don’t send news emails.

We count how this website is used, ourselves, with no analytics company and no cookies or other storage on your device. We do this only on the English, French, Spanish, Italian and Turkish versions of the site; the Finnish, Bulgarian and Arabic versions record nothing. For each page load we record the page, language and time, the buttons you click, your field-check answers and result, the form step you reach and whether sending worked, the campaign tag of the link you followed, the name of the website that sent you (not the full address) and whether your screen is mobile or desktop size. A random number held only in your browser's memory groups the clicks of one page view and disappears when you leave. We do not record your name, email or anything you type, these measurement records never contain your IP address, and we do not link visits to each other or to you. Detailed records are kept 90 days, then turned into daily totals kept up to 25 months. If your browser sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track, we record nothing. If you send a pilot request, the link's campaign tag, the referring website and your field-check result are stored with your request, so we know how you found us.

sections.h: Security log of our staff area
sections.p: Our website has a private area for CloverProof staff. If anyone, including a member of the public, signs in, tries to sign in or tries to use it, our security log records the time, what was attempted and whether it worked, a shortened IP address (the end of it removed) and the browser type (for example Firefox). It never records passwords, codes or anything typed into a form. To slow down password guessing we also keep counters based on a scrambled form of the shortened IP address and the email typed; they are deleted within two days. We use this only to keep the website secure. Only CloverProof administrators can see the log, and it is deleted automatically after 60 days. Until Canadian hosting is live it is stored in the United States by Railway. Ordinary visits to our public pages are not in this log. If you are in the EU, we rely on our legitimate interest in keeping the site secure, and you can object.

Our software proposes each plan. An AI system may help check it. The AI system never receives your name, contact details, address or exact field boundaries; it sees only de-identified case data. A named person then approves, changes or rejects every number before you see it: either our human agronomist or a CloverProof administrator who is not an agronomist. Your plan and its proof PDF show which of the two approved it and their name; we never call an administrator approval an agronomist review. An AI check alone never approves a plan. You make the final decision about what you apply.

If you agree, we keep a de-identified copy of pilot results (the engine's proposal vs the human agronomist's final numbers) to make the engine more accurate. We use only plans approved by our human agronomist, not plans approved by an administrator. Names, contact details, farm and field names and exact locations are removed. You can say no and still take part.

Only the CloverProof team members who need it, our human agronomist, our Canadian hosting provider, which will store pilot data in Canada, and Railway, a US company that hosts our website and, until Canadian hosting is live, stores website requests, website measurement data and the staff-area security log in the United States, as our service providers. No AI provider receives information that identifies you or your farm. We do not sell your information and we do not use advertising trackers or any analytics company.

Pilot farm data (contacts, farms, fields, soil tests, plans, reviews and proof PDFs) will be stored in Canada. We do not collect real pilot data into our hosted systems until that Canadian hosting is live. Until Canadian hosting is live, website requests and website measurement data are stored in the United States by our website host, Railway, a US company, where US authorities may be able to access them under US law. When Canadian hosting is live, this data moves to Canada and we will update this notice. We use data-processing contracts to protect your information.

Until the pilot selection is complete, or longer if you join the pilot. The staff-area security log is deleted automatically after 60 days, and the sign-in throttling counters within two days. You can ask us to delete your details at any time.

You can ask to see, correct or delete your information, ask how a number in your plan was produced and who approved it, and withdraw consent at any time. We reply within 30 days. You can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (priv.gc.ca) or, if you are in the EU, to your local data-protection authority.

check.title: What could your plan cover?
check.intro: Answer four quick questions. Each answer fills a leaf. At the end you'll see what kind of plan we could build for this field — before you share anything.

questions.q: Do you have a lab soil test for this field?
Does the report show the extraction method and sampling depth?
questions.hint: For example Olsen, Bray-1 or Mehlich-3, and the depth in cm or inches.

questions.q: Do you know what grew on this field last season?
Do you have a realistic yield target for this season?

full.title: A full nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium plan
full.body: With a complete lab report we can plan all three nutrients, each with its own confidence level and reasons.

confirm.title: A full plan, once we confirm the lab method
confirm.body: You have a soil test. We'll ask for the report so we can read the extraction method and depth — then plan all three nutrients.

nOnly.title: A nitrogen plan — and a soil test for the rest
nOnly.body: Without a lab test we only advise on nitrogen, at medium confidence at most. For phosphorus and potassium we'll recommend a test first.

gaps.previousCrop: Last season's crop — it changes how much nitrogen the soil already supplies.
gaps.target: A yield target — the plan is built around it.
gaps.method: The lab's extraction method and sampling depth.
gaps.soilTest: A lab soil test for phosphorus and potassium.

check.noGaps: Nothing missing. This field is ready for a plan.
check.cta: Request a pilot plan for this field
check.disclaimer: This check only shows the scope of a plan. It gives no rates — those come after an agronomist reviews your data.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.description: What CloverProof is working on now, what comes next and what comes later, in plain language.
roadmap.intro: What we are working on, what comes next and what comes later. This is a plan, not a promise: it will change as we learn from farmers and advisors.

status.title: Where we are today
status.text: CloverProof is at an early stage. Our planning tool is internal and is being tested with made-up farm data. Its agronomic values are not yet validated by a human agronomist, and no plan reaches a farmer until a human agronomist has approved it.

cta.title: Tell us what matters on your farm
cta.text: We want to hear from farmers and advisors before we build more. What you tell us can change this list.

now.title: Now
now.intro: Being built and tested by our team

items.title: Field-by-field wheat plans
items.text: A tool for our team that drafts a fertilizer plan for one field: what to apply, how much, when and why. We are starting with winter wheat in Ontario.

items.title: A person reviews every plan
items.text: An agronomist can approve, change or reject a draft. If a number changes, the reason is kept and the plan gets a new version.

items.title: Phosphorus and potassium from a lab test
items.text: With a lab soil test, a draft can cover these too, for the lab methods we have reference tables for. Without a test it covers nitrogen only, at medium confidence at most.

items.title: Checking the numbers
items.text: The values behind the drafts come from published guidance. A human agronomist still has to check them before they are used for a real farm.

items.title: First pilot plans
items.text: Requests are open. We plan to prepare plans for a small number of wheat farms in February–April 2027, each approved by a human agronomist before the farm sees it.

items.title: Timing that follows the season
items.text: Suggested application windows that take the season's weather into account and show when they were last updated.

items.title: Sending us your soil report
items.text: Share your lab report as a file. A person enters the values and confirms them.

items.title: Accounts for farmers and advisors
items.text: See your approved plans in one place. An advisor sees a farm only if the farmer gives access, and the farmer can take it back.

items.title: Recording what you applied
items.text: A simple, phone-friendly log of what was planned and what you actually did.

items.title: Sharing a proof document
items.text: Send a link to your proof document and turn it off when you no longer want it shared.

later.title: Later
later.intro: Depends on what we learn in the pilot

items.title: Fields on a map
items.text: Draw or upload field boundaries instead of typing the area.

items.title: Reading soil reports for you
items.text: Values filled in from your report for you to confirm. We will offer this only if it proves reliable enough.

items.title: Season results
items.text: Record the harvest and whether the plan was followed, so we can see where plans need to change.

items.title: A phone app
items.text: An app for use in the field, including where the signal is poor.

items.title: More crops and regions
items.text: Other crops and places, each with its own rules and its own review.

changelog.title: What's new
changelog.description: Recent changes to CloverProof, in plain language.
changelog.intro: Recent changes to CloverProof. Some are on this website. Others are in our internal tool, which farmers cannot use yet.

entries.title: Hectares or acres
entries.text: Rates in the internal tool can now be shown in kg/ha or lb/ac.

entries.title: A soil estimate when there is no lab test
entries.text: A field with no lab test can now show a published soil estimate as background. The plan stays nitrogen only, at medium confidence at most, and we still recommend a test.

entries.title: Phosphorus and potassium from lab tests
entries.text: Drafts can now include these nutrients when the lab used a method we have a reference table for.

entries.title: Nitrogen in several applications
entries.text: Drafts can divide nitrogen into several applications, with a suggested time for each. The timing values still need a human agronomist's check.

entries.title: CloverProof in Hebrew
entries.text: The website is now available in Hebrew. The translation is machine-made and is waiting for a native speaker's review.

entries.title: A record of each reviewed plan
entries.text: A reviewed test plan can now produce a PDF showing the inputs, the reasoning and who reviewed it.

entries.title: The website in eight languages
entries.text: You can read about CloverProof in English, French, Italian, Spanish, Bulgarian, Finnish, Turkish and Arabic. Translations are machine-made and are waiting for native speakers' review.

entries.title: A shorter pilot form
entries.text: We removed the free-text notes box, so we collect less about you.

entries.title: A two-minute field check
entries.text: Answer four quick questions and see what kind of plan we could build for a field, before you share anything.
